title: Swift or Exact? Boosting Efficient Microarchitecture DSE via Multi-fidelity Partial Order Prediction
problem: Microarchitecture design space exploration (DSE) is bottlenecked by slow synthesis and high-fidelity simulation (SPICE); early-stage PPA estimates are pessimistic and inaccurate, preventing rapid design iteration to find Pareto-optimal configurations.
motivation: High-fidelity simulation is expensive; early-stage estimates have low confidence; balancing accuracy and speed is critical for efficient architecture exploration.
method: The system combines quick-rough estimates with slow-accurate simulations using a Gaussian process, which is a statistical model that predicts outcomes and estimates its own uncertainty. It learns which rough estimates are reliable by comparing them to accurate results, then runs expensive accurate simulations only when it needs confirmation of uncertain designs. This avoids both the cost of always running slow simulations and the inaccuracy of relying only on rough estimates.
key_novelty: The core idea is a statistical model that explicitly treats rough and accurate estimates as different-quality information, then identifies the best designs by checking which options beat others rather than assigning exact scores.
contributions: Non-linear Gaussian process model for multi-stage fidelity fusion
Reliability assessment of low-fidelity data via logical regression and partial orders
Faster Pareto front approximation with better performance than direct DSE
Reduced high-fidelity simulation cost through intelligent low-fidelity reuse

metrics.other: Faster convergence to Pareto front, reduced high-fidelity evaluations

limitations: Evaluation context (specific architectures, node technology) not detailed; generalization to unconventional ISA designs or heterogeneous cores; interaction with power/thermal models not discussed.
primary_theme: multi-fidelity Gaussian process for efficient microarchitecture DSE
